content.title: Survivor 50’s Stephenie, 17 years ago: ‘it takes a lot for me to actually hate someone’
content.text: Survivor 50 player Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick is back for her fourth season—though when she played for a third time, on Survivor Heroes vs. Villains, she told me that was it: even if they tried to pay her $6 million, she’d say no. I interviewed her before the season, along with the other players, and am now presenting those interviews in full in advance of Survivor 50. As I wrote in the intro to this series, Stephenie is back in the news: Eliza Orlins criticized Stephenie LaGrossa for “engaging with xenophobic, anti-immigrant rhetoric”; Stephenie’s response to that was a video rant in which she said, “Don’t come at me with your political status when you’re fucking Jewish.” (That’s a hell of a way to defend yourself against charges of bigotry.) Stephenie has again apologized this week after Eliza resurfaced it. On Aug. 4, 2009, Stephenie talked about: Pre-season alliances: “They scared the living daylights out of us” Expectations for season 20 twists: “I think it’s gonna be totally ridiculous. I think it’s gonna be crazy” The mistake she made her season returning: “I just don’t think I was vocal enough about what moves I made and why I made them” Players she doesn’t like: “I don’t hate anyone. I don’t loathe anyone … It takes a lot for me to actually hate someone” Playing a fourth time: “My body cannot take any more. I don’t care if they try to pay me six million. Nope, this is it. So I better go out with a bang. “ Stephenie was voted out second from the heroes tribe. Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick Andy Dehnart: What brings you back to Survivor for number three? Stephenie LaGrossa: Done it twice and haven’t won yet, so a third time’s a charm. Just gonna try until you win. That’s right. No hesitation about doing it for a third time? Not really, but I wasn’t like, Yes! I was more like, Holy crap, I’m gonna do this again, really? I’m gonna put my body through this again? Obviously excited to do it, but you know, it’s scary because it’s been four years since I did the last one and five years since I did the one before that. So I’m a little older. I’m not in as great of shape as I was, but you know what? I never won, like I said, and I love to compete. I’m super competitive. And I think this time around, I have a good shot at winning. What gives you that better shot? The fact that I never won before is huge. I know it’s my third time and I know I was a sort of a big, one of the bigger personalities to play, but— …Never mind physical. (laughs) And I was pretty strong! But at the same time, you know, coming back, we’re all threats. I mean, this is basically an all-star. We’ve all played the game before. We’re all in the same boat. Some people have won the million, some people haven’t. So you really can’t rule out certain people just based on if they’re strong mentally, physically, if they won the million, this and that. I mean, but for me, I think I have a lot of things going my way. And if I align with the right people, get to the merge and the rest, hopefully it’ll be history. Let’s get to that in a second. You were mentioning about like not having won. Are you saying that the winners are targets? I think the winners will be targets actually, because I think people in this game try to use any little thing they can just to eliminate other people besides themselves. So I do think there’ll be targets. Tom Westman, who is one of my absolute favorites, is a winner and I will do everything in my power to try to keep him around and stick with him if I get the chance to align with him. Just because you like him as a person? And he’s honest. He’s somebody that’ll be honest. He’ll go with me to the end and he’ll be like, “Hey, whoever wins here.” Do you know him outside of the game? Well, he was on my first season. Right, right. So I knew him from that and then we kind of lost touch the past like four years. His wife is my Facebook friend, but I haven’t really talked to her. And you know, I’m just really—I haven’t seen him in like four years. So it’s really exciting for me to see him here. Just a familiar face. It’s like a little breath of fresh air because it feels like you have a little piece of home with you almost because you go out there and you just feel so alone because you know nobody. You don’t know anybody [else] here? Are you friends with anybody? I know them and I’ve met some of them, but I’m not friendly with them. I don’t—I’ve never really talked to them and really hung out with them. So for me, it’s kind of a whole new ball game. So no preseason alliances? I don’t have any, no. Does that worry you? I mean, if other people do… I know that all-stars, the first all-stars, everybody was aligned and the game was decided before they went in. And this time, I think they were really strategic with us in the casting process. They scared the living daylights out of us—just saying, if you align and we catch you, there’s an alternate waiting. So I didn’t want to jeopardize my chance. And also I’m trying to go in there, play, and as honest as I can, as hard as I can, and as real as I can. So if that means hit the beach running and try to align myself, then that’s what I’m gonna do. And if everyone’s already aligned and they don’t want to align with me, then so be it. But I’m ready to go in there and play an honest game. So is that your strategy? The same kind of thing that you’ve done before? My strategy is to play exactly how I played before. Don’t hide my strength. I’m a strong, competitive person. I’m not gonna hide that, I’m gonna be good around camp, I’m gonna hopefully be a nice person, a happy person, a fun person to be around, means a lot out there. It’s so brutal, you don’t want some annoying, ridiculous person like next to you constantly, so I don’t think I’m that type of person. So hopefully that’ll help, and also I think threading out the weak early on, that way if and when I get to the merge, I’m a strong player but everybody else there is strong as well—so it’s not like all, you know, let’s get rid of her ’cause she’s strong, because everybody’s gonna be strong at that point. Maybe get rid of the physically weak in the beginning. Kind of the reverse of the normal trajectory of a season? No, I always was wanting to get rid of the weak, but if someone who happens to be strong is totally obnoxious and you can’t stand them being around camp, we went with that too. But you always want to try to keep the strongest around because you’re never going to get to the merge if you don’t, because your team’s never going to win challenges and you’re, you know, you’re going to lose numbers. You need your numbers to get to the merge. Do you expect them to sort of keep the game pretty consistent for this season? Meaning? I mean, it’s the 20th season, like who knows what they have… No, I think it’s gonna be totally ridiculous. I think it’s gonna be crazy. I think that the challenges are gonna be absolutely ridiculous. I think that they’re gonna do stuff and we’re gonna be like, no friggin’ way. You can’t do that. And they’re like, yeah, we can, it’s Survivor. Anything goes. As much as I say I’m prepared, everyone’s like, “Well, you’ve done it before, so you know what to expect.” I’m like, “Yeah, that’s the bad thing. I know what to expect.” And you get out there and you’re like, “I can’t believe I’m doing this again.” But, no, I think it’s gonna be insane. I don’t know, they have something. We’re seeing the contestants, we can’t talk to them, but we’re seeing them. So that’s just too easy. People already have these preconceived notions of who they’re gonna line with. I mean, they have something up their sleeve. They’re gonna do something insane. Do you feel, I mean, because you’ve done it three times, do you feel like, are you kind of more ready to roll with those kind of punches? I think from the time I did it the first time to the second time, I improved dramatically, strategically, and in a game mindset. Having done it twice and coming back a third time, I think that’s really gonna work in my favor. Just mentally, because out there, it’s one thing to be physical, it’s one thing to stay healthy, but mentally, if you lose it mentally, you are done. Your brain is the most powerful thing in your whole body. And that’s why I did so well the first few times because mentally I kept it together where other people were losing it and this and that. I’m not a machine, I’m gonna cry, I’m gonna break down. It’s gonna be hard. But as long as you realize it’s six weeks out of your life, go out there, treat it as an amazing experience you’re never gonna get to do again and an amazing place you may never go again and look at it like that, I think I’ll be okay. I was gonna ask you—I think you kind of are getting to this—you went into Guatemala where you and Bobby Jon had this abnormal experience where you guys were crazy targets immediately. Crazy Because everyone knew who you were and they knew how strong you were, yet you still made it to the very, very end. Right. In Guatemala, I had to play much more of a strategic game because everyone knew who I was and knew what I was capable of. Bobby Jon as well. I was on the opposite team. I don’t know what he did over there. But we did get to the merge together and he was going to be one of the first people to go just because he didn’t have those strong alliances made. And (opens water bottle)—excuse me, I just ate a half a bagel, sorry— It’s okay! But I was forced to sort of play the game a little harder and lie a little bit. And it’s Survivor, you’re gonna do that. What wasn’t seen is that I lied to probably two people on that entire jury; the rest of the people I was very honest with but you didn’t see that when it comes out you know in on you know on TV—which is fine, they edit how they need to. But this time around, I will be strategic. I will be honest. I probably will fib a little, but at the same time, if and when I get to that final Tribal Council, I will voice why I did what I did—which I didn’t do the first time, which I think was a huge instrument me not winning the million dollars. I was thinking like if you’re replaying that in your mind, like, what did I do? Yeah, I just don’t think I was vocal enough about what moves I made and why I made them. I just was kind of like, Yeah, you know why I had a target on my back. Well, I didn’t explain why I had a target on my back and what that meant. So this time I’m really gonna go out there I’m gonna try to you—if I get to that point, it’s one step at a time! Let’s get past the first Tribal Council!—but if I get to that point, really address everyone individually. Gotcha. When you’re looking at this group, who are you excited to see? It just looks like a great group of people. I mean, there’s about three guys I really don’t know, and I really don’t even know their names. I think I know their names, but I just don’t know them. Are they from more recent seasons? Yeah, ’cause I kind of stopped watching after Fans vs. Favorites. I’ve been traveling a lot, and my life’s kind of been crazy, and I’ve just kind of been missing it. But you know, I’m really excited and I don’t even know these people that well. But I’m excited to see Rupert and Boston Rob and Colby; I’m super excited to see Tom. I, for a short time, interviewed Cirie and Candice on the red carpet, and Danielle So I met them briefly. It’s crazy. I really don’t know much about Sugar. I don’t know much about the other skinny blonde—I think her name’s Courtney I really don’t know much about Amanda. I think she got married to a guy—I don’t even know. One of them got married to another. So I don’t even know. It’s exciting—it’s just a fun group of people, you can tell, and that’s really important. So you don’t loathe anyone off the bat? Nope. There’s no one I loathe. I can see myself probably wanting to get rid of a few of the girls because they’re they’re very weak and, if they’re on my team, they’re probably not gonna help us physically just off bat. But then I don’t want to eliminate all the women and maybe I’m the only woman left, and the guys get rid of me. Who knows? That’s just kind of what I’m thinking now, but I don’t ever—I don’t hate anyone. I don’t loathe anyone. I mean, even on Palau—What was her name? She got on my nerves a little bit—Jolanda. She was the first person off, but she was a great person. To this day, we e-mail. It takes a lot for me to actually hate someone. Have you done anything specifically to prepare? The first time, I really trained hard. I knew two months in advance; I trained like a lunatic, personal trainer, this and that. The second time I went back just six months later. So physically, my body wasn’t ready. This time, we really just found out about a month ago It’s been a possibility maybe a month and a half, and then we found out like a month ago—maybe not even three weeks ago it was definite. So when it was a possibility, about, I guess, five weeks ago, I got a personal trainer, so I did start training. I have two sessions left—I didn’t even get a chance to finish all my sessions! So I’m certainly not in the shape that I would have liked to have been in. But I definitely ate a lot again, and just tried to put on… In everyday life I’d say I’d like to lose weight, but for this experience I’ve tried to put on just a couple, 5, 10 extra pounds. Probably make me look fat on camera, but whatever. Because you’re in high definition now, which you weren’t in your seasons. How about it? So that’s going to be cute. Hopefully I lose weight quick. But no, that’s what your body lives off of. These girls that go in and they’re 95, 105 pounds—it’s day six and they are breaking down. Physically, your body just cannot handle it. So I ate a lot and I worked out and mentally I’ve tried to prepare, and I said all my goodbyes, and I put that behind me. And now it’s like: game face and game on. What’s your life been like the past couple of years? It’s been awesome. After Survivor—I used to do pharmaceuticals, and I never went back to that because they wouldn’t hire me. They thought I’d leave again for TV. So I did some sales and that didn’t work out, and then I did some TV things—hosting red carpet events, some modeling, some magazine stuff, a few fitness videos. That was really cool but part of me never wanted to move to New York or LA and try to like make a life out of it. So about a year and a half ago, I bought a restaurant in Philadelphia with my brother. What’s it called? GiGi Restaurant and Lounge. It’s in Old City; we have the largest outside seating. And it’s there that I met my now-fiancé a year and a half ago. And he plays for the Philadelphia Phillies. He’s in the organization. He was up with them for a year and a half in the big leagues. He started this season in the AAA minor leagues. And as I left, he just pitched at Giants Stadium in San Francisco. So, he’s back in the big leagues, but anything can change. He’s young, so he has a while until he really makes it. I’m getting married and I have a restaurant and I live back in Philly now, in Seattle with him in the offseason. And it’s been great. I don’t really do that much TV stuff anymore, because I travel with him and I have a business. Has Survivor affected your life in any way? Oh yeah, it’s totally changed my life. It’s bizarre that people still come up to me and recognize me. It’s insane—it was insane right after both shows. I still get fan mail constantly and e-mails and just so many kind words like I was an inspiration to this little girl or this lady. And it’s just incredible, because I’m just some girl from Philadelphia who did pharmaceutical sales. And now I was on a reality show and have touched so many people’s lives. So that really means a lot to me. Interesting. This is a random question: There’s been a lot of pharmaceutical sales reps on the show. Is there something about that job? I think in order to be a pharmaceutical sales rep, you have to be a A-type personality. And I think that’s what they look for on shows like this because they’re so competitive. Any type of sales job, you have to have a pretty decent personality and you have to be pretty flexible and be able to sort of go with the flow and meet new people, but especially pharmaceutical sales because it’s so competitive and there’s so many people that want your job. So I mean, I think it’s just the type of personality that a person has coming out of that industry. But you’re right. I mean, even on The Bachelor, there’s a lot of pharmaceutical sales reps too. Yeah, that’s true. Let me think what else I wanted to ask you about… In terms of thinking about the game, and what you’ve learned from the past few times—we talked about that they might throw some things in there. Do you have some clear understanding of it now? I get this game and I know the path to victory. You know what? I think I do. But they throw so many things at you when you’re out there. I mean, any minute there could be a double elimination, any minute there could be no elimination, any minute they could switch the tribes up, any minute you could be stranded by yourself. So you think you know exactly what’s coming, but you never know. All I know is that, mentally, I need to stay strong. Physically, I need to be careful. And you have to be careful when you sit down—make sure you don’t sit on a scorpion. When you lay down, make sure you’re laying in a good spot. When you go to the bathroom, make sure there’s nothing out there that’s going to attack you. You have to be very cautious of your surroundings because it’s not like a movie set. It’s all very real. And if you get hurt, you’re screwed. Because that’s it. Game over for you. So my biggest thing is going to be to keep healthy out there as much as possible. Drink as much water as I can, even though it’s disgusting, drink it, and make sure my urine is somewhat clear, because you dehydrate, that’s another thing. And then just be smart and just mentally try to keep my head in the game. Did you do any research as to the place you may be going? You know what? I found out last week that it’s in Samoa; that’s what they told me. Now they could be freaking lying about that too, because I swear to God, they are trying to screw your mind over at any chance they get. But I know it’s beautiful there. I know it’s in the South Pacific. I’m guessing it’s very similar to Palau, which I absolutely love. I believe there’s a lot of fish and a lot of coconut—I hate coconut because I lived off of it. I hate coconut, but I’ll be eating it. I think they’re eight hours behind the East Coast time. I think they’re in a different time zone. So as far as the game beginning, if we fly out tonight, I actually think the game’s gonna start tomorrow. I have put thought into that. I think it’s gonna start Wednesday, the fifth, which means 39 days from there, it’ll be the 13th, which means I could be home three days after that. I’ve been trying to figure that all out too. But other than that, I mean, no, I really don’t know a ton about the place. You keep mentioning sort of stuff about the producers throwing in stuff. After having done it again twice, what have you picked up on? It’s all very real. I mean, they don’t— I’ve been on location three times in a row, so I’m very [familiar]… Right. But if you’re like, Oh, I want to get rid of this person, they will say to you, You think that’s a good idea? So they’ll make you second-guess yourself a little bit out there. And they know what type of person they want to portray you as. They have a little bit of an edit in mind. If they want to take more of your bitchy personality as opposed to your more calm personality or nicer personality, they will and they can. I’ve seen that just in the past few seasons. I went from America’s sweetheart to this like cutthroat bitch within a matter of a year, and I played the same exact game. But, you know, it was what it was. Do you go into those like interviews thinking, like, Okay, I’m not going to give them what I know they want. No, I’m always so honest. I go into the interviews and I’m brutally honest. I have a little bit of a bad mouth. I grew up with all boys and I have a little bit of diarrhea mouth, so I’m going to be cautious of that because nobody wants to hear a truck driver on TV come out of a girl. So I’ll be a little cautious of that. That could be a whole new personality trait. Yeah. Third personality trait. Stephanie the truck driver now. Stephanie the sweetheart, Stephanie the devil, Stephanie the truck driver. Excellent. And then the next all-stars you can come back and do something totally new. Right. No. (laughs) Third time is it for me. Is it? That is it. My body cannot take anymore. I don’t care if they try to pay me six million. Nope, this is it. So I better go out with a bang.
